VirtualTable

VirtualTable.Rd

A virtual table is a type of table that is dynamically built from a Synapse SQL query. Its content is read only and based off the defining_sql attribute. The SQL of the virtual table may NOT contain JOIN or UNION clauses and must reference a table that has a non-empty schema.

A VirtualTable object represents this VirtualTable API model in Synapse: <https://rest-docs.synapse.org/rest/org/sagebionetworks/repo/model/table/VirtualTable.html>

Usage

VirtualTable(id=NULL, name=NULL, parent_id=NULL, activity=NULL, version_number=NULL, description=NULL, etag=NULL, created_on=NULL, modified_on=NULL, created_by=NULL, modified_by=NULL, version_label=NULL, version_comment=NULL, is_latest_version=NULL, columns=list(), is_search_enabled=NULL, defining_sql=NULL, annotations=list())

Format

An S3-style class object.

Arguments

id

(Optional[str]) The unique immutable ID for this entity. Once issued, this ID is guaranteed to never change or be re-issued.

name

(Optional[str]) The name of this entity. Must be 256 characters or less. Names may only contain: letters, numbers, spaces, underscores, hyphens, periods, plus signs, apostrophes, and parentheses.

parent_id

(Optional[str]) The ID of the Entity that is the parent of this entity.

activity

(Optional[Activity]) The Activity model represents the main record of Provenance in Synapse.

version_number

(Optional[int]) The version number issued to this version on the object.

description

(Optional[str]) The description of this entity. Must be 1000 characters or less.

etag

(Optional[str]) Synapse employs an Optimistic Concurrency Control (OCC) scheme to handle concurrent updates. Since the E-Tag changes every time an entity is updated it is used to detect when a client's current representation of an entity is out-of-date.

created_on

(Optional[str]) The date this entity was created.

modified_on

(Optional[str]) The date this entity was last modified. In YYYY-MM-DD-Thh:mm:ss.sssZ format.

created_by

(Optional[str]) The ID of the user that created this entity.

modified_by

(Optional[str]) The ID of the user that last modified this entity.

version_label

(Optional[str]) The version label for this entity.

version_comment

(Optional[str]) The version comment for this entity.

is_latest_version

(Optional[bool]) If this is the latest version of the object.

columns

(Optional[OrderedDict[str, Column]]) (Read Only) The columns of a virtual table are dynamic based on the select statement of the definingSQL. This list of columnIds is for read-only purposes.

is_search_enabled

(Optional[bool]) When creating or updating a table or view specifies if full text search should be enabled.

defining_sql

(Optional[str]) The synapse SQL statement that defines the data in the virtual table. This field may NOT contain JOIN or UNION clauses. If a JOIN or UNION clause is present, a ValueError will be raised when the store method is called.

annotations

(Optional[dict[str, Union[list[str], list[bool], list[float], list[int], list[date], list[datetime]]]]) Additional metadata associated with the virtual table. The key is the name of your desired annotations. The value is an object containing a list of values (use empty list to represent no values for key) and the value type associated with all values in the list. To remove all annotations set this to an empty named list list() or NULL and store the entity.

Value

NULL

Methods

  • VirtualTable(id=NULL, name=NULL, parent_id=NULL, activity=NULL, version_number=NULL, description=NULL, etag=NULL, created_on=NULL, modified_on=NULL, created_by=NULL, modified_by=NULL, version_label=NULL, version_comment=NULL, is_latest_version=NULL, columns=list(), is_search_enabled=NULL, defining_sql=NULL, annotations=list()): Constructor for VirtualTable

  • synDeletePermissions(instance, include_self=TRUE, include_container_content=FALSE, recursive=FALSE, target_entity_types=NULL, dry_run=FALSE, show_acl_details=TRUE, show_files_in_containers=TRUE, synapse_client=NULL): Delete the entire local Access Control List (ACL) for a given Entity. This is not scoped to a specific user or group, but rather removes all permissions associated with the Entity. After this operation, the Entity will inherit permissions from its benefactor, which is typically its parent entity or the Project it belongs to.

    In order to remove permissions for a specific user or group, you should use the synSetPermissions() function with the access_type set to an empty list.

    By default, Entities such as FileEntity and Folder inherit their permission from their containing Project. For such Entities the Project is the Entity's 'benefactor'. This permission inheritance can be overridden by creating an ACL for the Entity. When this occurs the Entity becomes its own benefactor and all permission are determined by its own ACL.

    If the ACL of an Entity is deleted, then its benefactor will automatically be set to its parent's benefactor.

    Special notice for Projects: The ACL for a Project cannot be deleted, you must individually update or revoke the permissions for each user or group.

  • synGetAcl(instance, principal_id=NULL, check_benefactor=TRUE, synapse_client=NULL): Get the ACL that a user or group has on an Entity.

  • synGetPermissions(instance, synapse_client=NULL): Get the permissions that the caller has on an Entity.

  • synListAcl(instance, recursive=FALSE, include_container_content=FALSE, target_entity_types=NULL, log_tree=FALSE, synapse_client=NULL): List the Access Control Lists (ACLs) for this entity and optionally its children.

    This function returns the local sharing settings for the entity and optionally its children. It provides a mapping of all ACLs for the given container/entity.

    Important Note: This function returns the LOCAL sharing settings only, not the effective permissions that each Synapse User ID/Team has on the entities. More permissive permissions could be granted via a Team that the user has access to that has permissions on the entity, or through inheritance from parent entities.

  • synQuery(query, include_row_id_and_row_version=TRUE, convert_to_datetime=FALSE, download_location=NULL, quote_character="\"", escape_character=r"(\)", line_end="\n", separator=",", header=TRUE, timeout=250L, synapse_client=NULL): Query for data on a table stored in Synapse. The results will always be returned as a data frame unless you specify a download_location in which case the results will be downloaded to that location. There are a number of arguments that you may pass to this function depending on if you are getting the results back as a DataFrame or downloading the results to a file.

  • synQueryPartMask(query, part_mask, timeout=250L, synapse_client=NULL): Query for data on a table stored in Synapse. This is a more advanced use case of the synQuery() function that allows you to determine what additional metadata about the table or query should also be returned. If you do not need this additional information then you are better off using the synQuery() function.

    The query for this method uses this Rest API:
    <https://rest-docs.synapse.org/rest/POST/entity/id/table/query/async/start.html>

  • synSetPermissions(instance, principal_id=NULL, access_type=NULL, modify_benefactor=FALSE, warn_if_inherits=TRUE, overwrite=TRUE, synapse_client=NULL): Sets permission that a user or group has on an Entity. An Entity may have its own ACL or inherit its ACL from a benefactor.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
## Example 1: Create a new virtual table with a defining SQL query.
    library(synapser)
    synLogin()

    virtual_table = VirtualTable(
        name = "My Virtual Table",
        description = "A test virtual table",
        parent_id = "syn12345",
        defining_sql = "SELECT * FROM syn67890"
    ) |> synStore()
    cat("Created Virtual Table with ID:", virtual_table$id, "\n")

## Example 2: Update the defining SQL of an existing virtual table.
    library(synapser)
    synLogin()

    virtual_table = VirtualTable(id = "syn12345") |> synGet()
    virtual_table$defining_sql = "SELECT column1, column2 FROM syn67890"
    virtual_table = virtual_table |> synStore()
    cat("Updated Virtual Table defining SQL.\n")

## Example 3: Delete a virtual table.
    library(synapser)
    synLogin()

    virtual_table = VirtualTable(id = "syn12345")
    synDelete(virtual_table)
    cat("Deleted Virtual Table.\n")

## Example 4: Query data from a virtual table.
    library(synapser)
    synLogin()

    query_result = synQuery(query = "SELECT * FROM syn66080386")
    query_result
} # }
